initialization_coupling.issue_character: Two distinct initialization problems coexist: (1) setup_logging() is called at module scope in scripts, creating log files on disk as an import-time side effect; and (2) the logging namespace is fragmented — some modules use logging.getLogger(__name__) (publish, legacy_import, validation) while others use get_logger('batch_processing'), meaning the configured file handler silently misses log output from half the codebase.
initialization_coupling.score_rationale: The codebase avoids the worst initialization coupling patterns (no DB/network at import time, no circular init dependencies), but has a genuine fragmentation problem in logging namespaces: setup_logging() configures only the 'batch_processing' logger, yet half the src modules log to their own __name__ namespace which is not a child of 'batch_processing'. This means the configured file handler silently drops production logs from publish, validation, and legacy_import. Additionally, module-scope setup_logging() calls in scripts create log files on disk as import-time side effects, breaking test isolation. These are real operational and testability problems that would be discovered in practice, landing this in the 60s.

issues.summary: setup_logging() called at module scope in scripts creates a timestamped log file on disk as an import-time side effect
evidence: generate_all_outputs.py line 48: `logger = setup_logging()` at module scope
import_legacy_materials.py line 40: `logger = setup_logging()` at module scope
setup_logging() in logging_config.py lines 46-57 creates log_dir, then a timestamped log file via FileHandler — this disk I/O executes at import time
Any test or tool that imports these scripts (e.g., subprocess or pytest) will create spurious log files
issues.suggestion: Move setup_logging() calls into the main() function of each script, after argument parsing. Module-scope loggers should call get_logger() only: `logger = get_logger('batch_processing')`. setup_logging() should be called exactly once in the entry point: `def main(): logger = setup_logging(); ...`

issues.summary: Half of src modules log to __name__ namespaces not under 'batch_processing', silently bypassing the file handler configured by setup_logging()
evidence: src/validation/main.py line 30: `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` — logs to 'src.validation.main'
src/legacy_import/main.py line 16: `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` — logs to 'src.legacy_import.main'
src/publish/main.py line 11: `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` — logs to 'src.publish.main'
setup_logging() in logging_config.py line 29: `logger = logging.getLogger('batch_processing')` — only configures 'batch_processing' namespace

Python logging propagates child→parent: 'batch_processing.foo' would propagate to 'batch_processing', but 'src.publish.main' does not — it propagates to root logger which has no file handler configured
issues.suggestion: Standardize all src modules to use `logger = logging.getLogger('batch_processing.' + __name__.split('.')[-1])` or pass a logger via dependency injection. Alternatively, configure setup_logging() to also add a handler to the root logger so all namespaces benefit from file logging.

issues.summary: Module-scope get_logger() calls in src modules silently return unconfigured loggers if imported before setup_logging() is called
evidence: batch_processing/main.py line 19: `logger = get_logger()` at module scope
html_website/main.py line 20: `logger = get_logger('html_website')` at module scope
get_logger() returns logging.getLogger(name) with no check whether handlers have been configured
If any test imports batch_processing.main without first calling setup_logging(), all logger.info/debug calls silently produce no output and no file
issues.suggestion: Add a lazy initialization guard in get_logger(): check if the returned logger has no handlers and no parent handlers, and if so call setup_logging() with defaults. Alternatively, document the ordering requirement in get_logger()'s docstring with a warning: 'Call setup_logging() before first use in scripts.'

issues.summary: Lazy function-body imports in legacy_import/main.py indicate latent circular dependency pressure in the import graph
evidence: Line 41: `from src.format_conversion.utils import convert_docx_to_markdown` inside process_chapter_questions() function body
Line 408: `from src.format_conversion.main import convert_file` inside create_for_upload_files() function body
Line 399: `from src.markdown_to_pdf.main import render_markdown_to_pdf` inside create_for_upload_files() function body
These are deferred to avoid import-time issues, suggesting that moving them to module scope would cause circular imports or slow startup
issues.suggestion: Investigate whether the lazy imports can be moved to module scope by restructuring legacy_import to depend on format_conversion at the package boundary. If circular dependency is confirmed, document it with a comment explaining why the lazy import is necessary. This also affects testability — lazy imports make mock injection harder.

root_causes: setup_logging() was designed for scripts as a setup function, but its use as a module-scope assignment carried its file-creation side effect into import time.

The logging namespace fragmentation arises because different modules were written independently — some following the batch_processing convention, others using standard __name__ logging — without a enforced convention.
possible_false_positives: lazy_imports_circular_pressure is medium confidence — the lazy imports may be an intentional performance optimization rather than a circular dependency workaround.
